sentences.text: 1. Ms. Madhu Sharma, the sole appellant, after invoking the provisions of the provisions of Sec. 372 CrPC, preferred the above criminal appeal and challenges the impugned judgment/order dated 17.05.2019 passed by ld. MM whereby acquitting the accused Veena stood acquitted for the offences alleged against her.
2. It is also to be mentioned here that along with the present criminal appeal an application under Sec. 5 of Limitation Act was also filed.
3. Notice of the present criminal appeal along with the application was issued to the respondents.
TCR was also summoned.
4. Arguments on the present matter heard.
Record including the relevant judgment also perused.

5. Qua application on condonation of delay, ld. counsel prayed for condoning the delay of around 85 days on various ground stating that firstly, appellant is an old lady and fully dependent on her husband for financial assistance and later on suffered with eye problem and when contacted her counsel, mother of counsel expired and then appeal was filed with such a delay period.
Ld. counsel prayed for condoning the delay.

6. On merits of the present criminal appeal, it is contended by ld. counsel for the appellant that the impugned judgment/order suffers from patent illegality, perversity, arbitrary and even not sustainable in the eyes of law further contending that same has been passed without considering the entire facts and material on record.
One of the contentions of the ld. counsel for the appellant is that judgment dated 17.05.2019 is totally based on surmises and conjectures and hence prayed for setting aside of the same.
7. Respondent no. 2 hotly contested the present criminal appeal and application under Sec. 5 of Limitation Act on all grounds.

His first contention is that even the present criminal appeal is not maintainable as the victim has no right to prefer the present appeal before the Court of Sessions and has only remedy to prefer the appeal before Hon'ble High Court after taking Leave and as such,
prayed for dismissal of the present criminal appeal only on this count.

On this issue, reliance has been placed on the cases reported as Satya Pal Singh Vs. State of MP [Crl. Appeal No. 1315 of 2015 decided on 06.10.2015 by Hon'ble Apex Court and Subhash Chand Vs. State [Crl. Appeal No. 50 of 2013 decided on 08.01.2013 by Hon'ble Apex Court] and ld. counsel drew the attention of the court towards the paragraph number 21 of judgment titled as Subhash Chand (supra).
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Subhash Chand Vs. State [Crl. Appeal No. 50 of 2013

sentences.text: Countering the said arguments, ld. counsel for the appellant placed reliance on the cases reported as S. Ganapathy Vs. N. Senthilvel [Crl. A (MD) No. 99 of 2015] decided on 05.04.2016 by Hon'ble High Court of Madras urging that present criminal appeal is maintainable.

entities.text: S. Ganapathy Vs. N. Senthilvel [Crl. A (MD) No. 99 of 2015]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further contended by ld. counsel for the appellant that present criminal appeal be allowed and impugned order/judgment dated 17.05.2019 be set aside after condoning the delay in preferring the present criminal appeal.
9. First of all, court will deal with this aspect of condonation of delay in preferring the criminal appeal.

Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153084365/
2 10.

entities.text: Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It must be remembered that in every case of delay, there can be some lapse on the part of the litigant concerned.
That alone is not enough to turn down his pleas and to shut the door against him.
If the explanation does not smack of malafides or it is not put forth as part for a dilatory strategy, the court must show utmost consideration to the suitor.
But when there is reasonable ground to think that the delay was occasioned to be the party deliberately to gain time, then the court should lean against acceptance of the explanation.
While condoning the delay, the court should not forget the opposite party altogether.
It must be borne in mind that he is loser and he too would have incurred quite large litigation expenses.
It would be a salutary guideline that when courts condone the delay due to latches on the part of the applicant, the court shall compensate the opposite party for his loss.

In case reported as AIR 2014 SC 746 titled as Basawaraj & Anr. Vs The Spl. Land Acquisition Officer, Hon'ble Apex Court observed as - Condonation of delay without considering the most relevant factor i.e. "sufficient cause" only on the condition that applicant would be deprived of interest for the delay period is most in appropriate.

entities.text: Basawaraj & Anr. Vs The Spl. Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where a case has been presented in the Court beyond limitation, the applicant has to explain the court as to what was the "sufficient cause" which means an adequate and enough reason which prevented him to approach the Court within limitation.
No court could be justified in condoning such an inordinate delay by imposing any condition whatsoever.
The application is to be decided only within the parameters laid down by Court in regard to the condonation of delay.

In case there was no sufficient cause to present a litigant to approach the Court on time condoning the delay without any justification, putting any condition whatsoever, amounts to passing an order in violation of the statutory provisions it tantamounts to showing utter disregard to the legislature.
(Para 7,15)
11. In the present neither any document has been placed in support of his contentions nor sufficient cause is there to condone the delay in preferring the present criminal appeal and

as such, with the above discussion and in the interests of justice, this court is of the view that there is no sufficient cause furnished by the appellant that gross negligence and deliberate in action as well as found lack of bondafide input for setting the condonation of delay and as such, this criminal appeal is liable to be dismissed only on the count of codonation.
12. Apart from that now court will deal with the issue of maintainability.
13. On the issue of maintainability, both parties hotly contested the matter and placed their reliance on the cases mentioned above.

14. This Court has gone through the provisions of Sec. 372 CrPC as amended in 2009 as well as Sec.
378 (4) CrPC.

As per provisions of Sec. 378 (4) CrPC, an appeal against the order of acquittal passed in criminal complaint can be filed only before concerned High Court after seeking Special Leave to Appeal and as such the appeal against the impugned judgment/order passed in criminal complaint case filed by the appellant/complainant is not maintainable under Sec. 372 CrPC as amended in 2009 because the provisions of Sec. 372 CrPC as amended in 2009 and 378 (4) CrPC are to be interpreted harmoniously.

If the present criminal appeal against the impugned judgment/order of acquittal in a criminal complaint case is held to be maintainable under Section 372 CrPC, then the Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153084365/
3 provisions of Sec. 378 (4) CrPC would be rendered nugatory and useless which could never be the intention of the legislature when Section 372 CrPc was amended in 2009.

entities.text: Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. In a case reported as The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. Vs. Sushil Kumar, Crl. A. No. 972/2012 decided on 03.09.2014.

entities.text: Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. Vs. Sushil Kumar, Crl. A. No. 972/2012
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
in its paras 13 to 16 Hon'ble court observed as:
"In my considered view, the "complaint" in the proceedings under Sec. 138 N.I. Act cannot be considered "victim" in the letter and spirit of the definition of Sec. 2 (wa) of the Code and definition of "injury" under Section 44 IPC cannot be imported into Sec. 138 N.I. Act.
In every such proceedings, at first instance, every complainant considers/claims himself/herself a "victim".

The complainant in these proceedings cannot be taken at par with those who put criminal law into motion to bring the offenders to book at whose hands, they have sustained "injury" as defined in Sec. 44 IPC.
The changes in CrPC were for "victims" who were the worst sufferers in a crime and did not have much role in the Court proceedings.
To avoid distortion of the Criminal Judicial System, they were given certain rights.
The controversy now is no longer res integra in view of the pronouncement of law by Supreme Court in "Subhash Chand Vs. State (Delhi Administration).(2013) 2 SCC 17.

entities.text: Subhash Chand Vs. State (Delhi Administration).(2013) 2 SCC 17
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was a complaint case under Sec. 7 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, in which Subhash Chand was tried and he was acquitted by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate.
The State filed criminal appeal before the Sessions Court under Sec. 378 (1) (a) CrPC.
Preliminary objections regarding maintainability of the appeal before the Sessions Court was rejected.
That order was challenged before this court (Delhi High Court) and it was held that Sessions Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the appeal.

The order of the High Court was challenged before the Supreme Court who remanded the case to this court for fresh decision after taking into consideration the provisions of Sections 378 (1) and 378 (4) and the relevant provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

After remand, this Court held that the appeal filed by the State against an order of acquittal would lie to the Sessions Court under Se. 378 (1) of the CrPC Again this order was challenged by the accused before the Supreme Court and Supreme Court held: ...we conclude that a complainant can file an application for special leave to appeal against an order of acquittal of any kind only to the High Court.
He cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court.
The complainant can challenge the order of acquittal by filing an application for special leave to appeal in the Delhi High Court and not in the Sessions Court...
16. Of course, the scope of Sec. 372 CrPC and subsequent amendments in CrPC, Act 2008 (Act 5 Of 2009) did not come for consideration before the Supreme Court in this case.
But it cannot be assumed that the Supreme Court was not aware of the existence of the provisions of Sec. 372.

The Supreme Court further observed:
"Thus, whether a case is a case instituted on a complaint depends on the legal provisions relating to the offence involved therein.

But once it is a case instituted on a Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153084365/
4 complaint and an order of acquittal is passed, whether the offence is bailable,
non-bailable, cognizable or non- cognizable, the complainant can file an application under Sc. 378 (4) for special leave to appeal against it in the High Court.

entities.text: Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 378 (4) places no restriction on the complainant..."

17. In another case reported as Bhavuben Dineshbhai Makwana V. State of Gujarat & Ors 2013 Crl LJ 4225, Full Bench of Gujarat High Court answering the reference on question number (3) "if the victim prefers an appeal before this court, challenging the acquittal, invoking his right under proviso to section 372 of CrPC, whether that appellant is required to first seek leave of the Court, as is required in case of appeal being preferred by the State?, held - "if the victim also happens to be the complainant and the appeal is against the acquittal, he is required to take leave as provided in Sec.
378 of the Criminal Procedure Code but if he is not the complainant, he is not required to apply for or obtain any leave.

entities.text: Bhavuben Dineshbhai Makwana V. State of Gujarat & Ors 2013 Crl LJ 4225
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Full Bench of Gujarat High Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
For the appeal against inadequency of compensation or punishment on a lesser offence, no leave is necessary at the instance of a victim, whether he is the complainant or not."
18.

In case reported as Subhash Chand (supra), Hon'ble Apex Court observed as - "...In view of the above, we conclude that a complainant can file an application for special leave to appeal against an order of acquittal of any kind only to the High Court.
He cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court.

In the instant case the complaint alleging offences punishable under Sec 16(1)(1A) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act and the Rules filed by complainant Shri Jaiswal, Local Health Authority through Delhi Administration.
The appellant was acquitted by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The complainant can challenge the order of acquittal by filling an application for special leave to appeal in the Delhi High Court and not in the Sessions Court.
Therefore, the impugned order holding that his case is not governed by Section 378 (4) of the Code is quashed and set aside.
In the circumstances the appeal is allowed."

19. No doubt, during the course of arguments, ld counsel for the appellant/complainant has also relied upon case, as mentioned above but it is clear that same is of no help to the appellant/complainant in the present matter in view of the judgment relied upon by the respondent which give more strength to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
20. With the above discussion, this court is of the view that present appeal is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed only on this count as well.
21. However, leaving aside all these above mentioned issues, now court will deal with the merits of the present above mentioned criminal appeal.
22. Perusal of the impugned order/judgment dated 17.05.2019, it is clear that ld. trial court passed the said judgment in detail after discussing each and every material placed on record.

It is also crystal clear that said impugned judgment has passed taking support of the judgments as mentioned therein and this court is the view that said impugned judgment/order does not suffer from any illegality, perversity and/or infirmity and as such, does not require any interference.

Accordingly,
Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153084365/
5 said impugned judgment dated 17.05.2019 stands upheld.

25. Appeal file be consigned to RR.
